etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English tellere (“one who counts or enumerates; one who recounts or relates; teller”), equivalent to tell (verb) +‎ -er.

definitions.definition: (banking, chiefly US) A bank clerk who receives and pays out money.
(more generally) A cashier at any place of business.

quote.citation: 2007, Joseph T. Wells, Corporate Fraud Handbook: Prevention and Detection, page 107:
quote.text: In the case discussed above, for example, the employee who stole money did so by waiting until another teller was on break, then logging on to that teller's register, ringing a “no sale,” and taking the cash.

quote.citation: 2013, Alastair Henry, Awakening in the Northwest Territories:
quote.text: The young femail teller fingered the prices into the cash register at great speed with great dexterity while simultaneously holding a conversation with the teller in the next lane.
The main street was shuttered; the only sign of life she detected was behind the window of the petrol station, where the teller was counting the day's cash balance into the till.

definitions.definition: A person who counts the votes in an election.
